experiment: M9b: the sampling-order part of M9 on a sum with identical Hessians

definitions.model: f_i(W) = ||W - y_i||^2 / 2 + (lam/2)||W||^2 on K x 1 matrices (x_i = 1): identical Hessians; the polar factor of the estimator is the estimator divided by its norm
definitions.D: the design of part D of M9 on the model instance (definitions/order of M9_summary.json), with lr_0 divided by step_scale = max(1, K/d)^(1/2) so that the total step length is path_factor x ||W_*||_op; level_over_reference = median C at each rho of the grid over the reference level
definitions.D_vs_M9: rho_star on the model next to rho_star on soft-mem and ls-mem (M9_summary.json, D/<instance>/cells/<b>/schemes/<scheme>/rho_star), by batch size and scheme; passes_at_fastest_rho = median passes to the target of part D (relative squared distance 1e-9, extra refreshes charged) at the rho with the smallest median among those where every seed reaches it (fastest/median of the same cells)
definitions.L: batch one, runs of 80 passes of `model_run` (20 runs per point, error coordinates, lam = 0, E_0 a unit vector, eta_0 = 4 ||E_0|| (1 - q^(1/n))); x = log(1/rho) = nats of lr^2 lost per pass; level = ||E||^2 / eta^2 at the end of a pass; a run is on schedule at a horizon if its level is at most 100 x the median level at x_ref = log(1/0.61) at that horizon (x_star_clean: 10 x); x_star = largest x of the grid with at least 0.8 of the runs on schedule (x_star_monotone: and at every smaller x of the grid); rate_second_half = slope per pass of the median log level over the second half of the run (0: on schedule; x: frozen iterate)
definitions.linear_saga: exponents of linear SAGA on the same model with the same n, read from the experiment B4b of the main study (None when results/B4b_summary.json is absent): typical_iid = largest pooled exponent of single runs under independent sampling over the steps tried there (at_c: gamma n lambda of that step); expectation_iid_at_that_c = exact exponent of the expected squared error at that step; reshuffled_mean_square_best = largest exact mean-square exponent under reshuffling over the same steps
